title: Extended Care Health Option (ECHO) Benefit Limits, Payment Order and Claim Filing Schedule
content:
Extended Care Health Option (ECHO) claims are paid against an annual benefit limit and in a fixed order of payers. The figures and terms in this schedule are the same in all ten ECHO tiers, from Extended Care Health Option, Sponsor E-1 to E-5 through Extended Care Health Option, Sponsor O-9 and O-10.

## Schedule A: the fiscal-year benefit cap

| Term | Every tier |
|---|---|
| Fiscal-year benefit cap: government share for all ECHO benefits other than ECHO Home Health Care, per beneficiary per federal fiscal year | USD 36000.00 |
| Year the cap is counted over | the federal fiscal year, October 1 to September 30 |
| Whether family members share one cap | no; each beneficiary has a cap of their own |
| Who pays charges above the cap | the sponsor family |
| Whether ECHO Home Health Care payments count toward the fiscal-year benefit cap | no |
| Separate annual limit on ECHO Home Health Care | the annual amount TRICARE would pay for skilled nursing facility care in the locality |

## Schedule B: order of payment and rounding

| Term | Every tier |
|---|---|
| Services the basic TRICARE program covers must be paid by the basic program, not ECHO | yes |
| Other health insurance pays before ECHO | yes |
| Rounding of the government share | to the cent |

## Schedule C: claim filing

| Term | Every tier |
|---|---|
| Calendar days after the date of service within which an ECHO claim must be received | 365 |

## Notes on the schedules

1. The cap of 36000.00 is a per-beneficiary amount. Two registered children of one sponsor each have their own 36000.00 for the same federal fiscal year; one child's payments never reduce the other's.
2. The cap year is the federal fiscal year, which runs from October 1 through the following September 30; it is not the calendar year.
3. ECHO Home Health Care is outside the 36000.00 cap and is limited instead by the annual amount TRICARE would pay for skilled nursing facility care in the locality.
4. Charges above the cap are the sponsor family's to pay.
5. The filing period is counted in calendar days from the date of service, and it is the date the claim is received that is measured against the 365 days.

*Hypothetical filing illustrations, for illustration only:* a claim received 200 calendar days after the date of service is within the 365-day filing period; a claim received 400 calendar days after the date of service is outside it.
